construct: file staleness recovery — the ability to reject an edit that references an outdated content tag, emit a rejection signal, then recover by re-reading the file and retrying with the updated tag.

input.description: The agent reads a file (obtaining a content tag), then the file is externally modified (changing the tag), then the agent attempts to edit using the old tag.
setup: External write to src/app.ts changes tag to #c3d4
edit('src/app.ts', anchor='#a1b2', oldText='status: draft', newText='status: reviewed') is rejected
signal store records one hashline stale-tag rejection
edit('src/app.ts', anchor='#c3d4', oldText='status: draft', newText='status: reviewed') succeeds

expectedBehavior: Hashline Patcher rejects the first edit due to tag mismatch and writes a stale-tag rejection signal. The agent then re-reads the file, retries with the updated tag, and the final file contains status reviewed with all other lines preserved.
passCondition: hashline_rejection_count == 1 AND signal_store_event_count >= 1 AND reread_after_rejection_count >= 1 AND retry_edit_success_count == 1 AND file_content_correctness == true
failureImplication: The agent or harness may either silently bypass stale-tag rejection or fail to recover after a legitimate stale edit rejection.
relatedPaper: AEvo Table 3: removing isolation lets 2/3 runs reward-hack.
regressionRisk: Changes to SnapshotStore update logic, tag comparison algorithm, or edit-patch routing could bypass the staleness check.
